title: bug: every FileWatcher reload restarts the periodic sweep timers, so a busy fleet can starve the self-heal sweeps
description:
DEFECT, filed by the governor on 2026-09-17 from live measurement. Nothing is stalled yet; so far it has only delayed one self-heal by about 4 minutes.

MECHANISM (source at HEAD, same as the live 09-13 dist)
- StateManager.load() ends by calling startBlockedTimeoutCheck, startProposalPurgeInterval, startStaleWorkerWatcher and startReconcileWindowCheck (packages/moe-daemon/src/state/StateManager.ts:1139-1142).
- Each start* first calls its stop* and then a fresh setInterval (src/state/sweeps.ts:58, 87, 124, 147), so the sweep's phase starts again from zero.
- The FileWatcher callback in src/index.ts calls state.load() on every .moe change that self-write suppression lets through.
- Net effect: after every reload, a 5-minute sweep needs another 5 reload-free minutes before it fires, and the 60s stale-worker watcher needs 60s.

WHAT TRIGGERED RELOADS (observed)
- The observed reloads followed claim_next_task.
- Self-write suppression (src/state/FileWatcher.ts:22, 52-54, 98-99) is a Set keyed by path. An entry is deleted on the first matching event and expires after 500ms.
- The claim writes the task file twice about 180ms apart, and the worker file three times within about 400ms. With awaitWriteFinish stabilityThreshold 100, that can produce two chokidar events for a single Set entry, and the second one reloads.
- Each reload also broadcasts an unfiltered STATE_SNAPSHOT (ARCHIVED tasks included: 308 tasks vs 171 on connect).

EVIDENCE, 2026-09-17
Live daemon pid 22572 started 16:44:23Z; passive /ws listener attached.
1. The reconcile-window sweep closed its past-window attempts at 16:53:38.35Z. These were attempt-fcb4df2f, attempt-6f430bd3 and attempt-91637830, all with lastPhaseAt 2026-09-15, so they had been eligible since boot. The boot-armed tick, due by 16:49:23Z, never acted. 16:53:38Z is exactly 5 minutes after architect-259309b5's claim at 16:48:37.9Z.
2. worker-3b5de06f's claim wrote files between 16:53:57.56Z and 16:53:57.96Z. The reload's STATE_SNAPSHOT broadcast went out at 16:53:58.102Z. The blocked-timeout sweep's Layer-3 prune of worker-a7127038 then emitted its STATE_SNAPSHOT at 16:58:58.101Z, exactly 5:00.000 later.

CONSEQUENCE
If fleet-wide claims (or any other unsuppressed .moe writes) arrive more often than every 5 minutes, these never run:
- checkBlockedTimeouts: blocked-timeout alerts and parking, the resource lease reaper, the stale-worker prune, and the REVIEW self-heal for a crashed QA
- runReconcileWindowSweep
If reloads arrive more often than every 60s, the stale-worker alerts also go silent. These are the recovery paths for dead seats.

DIRECTION (the architect decides)
- Arm each sweep once per process instead of re-arming it on every load(). For example, load() skips any start* whose interval is already armed, or index.ts arms the sweeps once after the first load.
- Keep the outside-the-lock arming and the mutex.exit detachment described in the load() comment.
- Reloads do not need re-arming: the sweep intervals are constants, and thresholds are read from state at tick time.
- Tightening self-write suppression (for example a per-path pending-write count) is a possible follow-up, not required here.
definitionOfDone: A FileWatcher-driven state.load() does not restart an already-armed sweep interval: a fake-timer test shows a load() 4 minutes after arming does not push back the 5-minute blocked-timeout and reconcile-window ticks, or the 60s stale-worker tick. The test fails on HEAD.

The first load() still arms every sweep outside the locked section, still detached via mutex.exit, and stop()/shutdown still clears every interval; the existing sweeps and StateManager tests stay green.
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md or the load() comment states that the sweeps are armed once per process and that reloads do not reset them.
npm test and npx tsc --noEmit pass in packages/moe-daemon.
taskRails: Do not introduce any idle-based release of WORKING/PLANNING tasks; only sweep scheduling changes.

implementationPlan.description:
Phases 1+2 — confirm the mechanism in source and record the baseline. No repo edits.

Verified while planning; re-check by grep, never by line number:
- `StateManager.load()` ends by calling `this.startBlockedTimeoutCheck()`, `this.startProposalPurgeInterval()`, `this.startStaleWorkerWatcher()` and `this.startReconcileWindowCheck()`, under a comment explaining why they are armed OUTSIDE the locked section and detached via `mutex.exit`.
- Each `start*` in state/sweeps.ts begins with its own `stop*` and then a fresh `setInterval`, so every call restarts the phase from zero. That is correct for an explicit caller and wrong for a reload.
- The ONLY non-test callers are those four lines in load(). The only test caller is sweeps.test.ts's 'arms one interval and genuinely clears it on stop', which deliberately calls `stopReconcileWindowCheck` first — so keeping the restart semantics of `start*` breaks nothing.
- `state.stop()` clears all four handles, so a later load() re-arms from scratch. That must keep working.

Check one thing the card's DIRECTION asserts, rather than assuming it: that a reload genuinely has nothing to re-read. Walk each tick closure and say in the step note which values are captured at ARM time and which are read from `state` at TICK time. Measured expectation: `checkBlockedTimeouts` and `checkReconcileWindow` read `state.staleWorkerTimeoutMs` / `state.reviewStaleTimeoutMs` / `state.reconcileWindowMs` at tick time, while `startStaleWorkerWatcher` captures `livenessTimeoutMs` in its closure — but load() always arms it with the default, so arming once freezes exactly the value a re-arm would have restored. If any closure turns out to capture a settings-derived value that a reload would legitimately change, say so before writing code; that would change the fix.

Baseline: `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` and `npx tsc --noEmit`, with counts.
implementationPlan.note:
No repo edits. Mechanism confirmed at HEAD 7728e7b by grep:
- StateManager.load() tail (after `await withTimeout(loadOperation, ...)`, outside the lock) calls this.startBlockedTimeoutCheck/startProposalPurgeInterval/startStaleWorkerWatcher/startReconcileWindowCheck. Those four lines are the ONLY non-test callers of start*.
- Each start* in state/sweeps.ts calls its own stop* and then `state.mutex.exit(() => setInterval(...))` + unref, so every call restarts the phase. Only 4 setInterval calls exist in non-test src, all in sweeps.ts.
- FileWatcher callback in src/index.ts: `await state.load(); wsServer.broadcast(STATE_SNAPSHOT)`.
- PLAN CORRECTION: StateManager has no `stop()`. The method that clears all four handles is `clearEmitter()` (calls the four stop*, then clears subscribers/emitter); index.ts shutdown calls `state.clearEmitter()`. The tests will use clearEmitter().
- Only test caller of start*: sweeps.test.ts 'arms one interval and genuinely clears it on stop' (stops first, then arms 60_000). StateManager.test.ts 'purges stale resolved proposals on load and starts purge interval' checks proposalPurgeInterval defined after load and undefined after clearEmitter.

Arm-time vs tick-time walk:
- blocked-timeout tick: `state.checkBlockedTimeouts()` captures nothing but `state`; runBlockedTimeoutSweep reads state.blockedTimeoutMs (readonly, ctor), state.reviewStaleTimeoutMs and state.staleWorkerTimeoutMs at TICK time.
- reconcile tick: `state.checkReconcileWindow()` captures nothing; runReconcileWindowSweep reads state.reconcileWindowMs at TICK time.
- proposal purge tick: `state.purgeResolvedProposals()` reads the module constant PROPOSAL_PURGE_AGE_MS (env at import) and state.proposals; load() also runs a purge inline on every load.
- stale-worker tick: captures `livenessTimeoutMs` at ARM time, but load() always arms via the wrapper defaults (60_000, 120_000). It is not settings-derived, so arming once freezes exactly what a re-arm would restore.
- Cadences are constants (300000, PROPOSAL_PURGE_INTERVAL_MS, 60_000, RECONCILE_WINDOW_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS). No closure captures a settings-derived value, so the plan's fix stands unchanged.

Baseline (packages/moe-daemon): `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0; `npm test` exit 0, 122 files, 2107 passed (2107). Per file: sweeps.test.ts 10/10, StateManager.test.ts 115/115, StateManager.fixes 7/7, FileWatcher.test 11/11, FileWatcher.paths 7/7, server/* 5+21+15+30+2+9+26+7. EOL: sweeps.ts CRLF; StateManager.ts and sweeps.test.ts LF (use Edit, which keeps EOL).
Shared checkout has ~28 peer-dirty paths (docs/*, .moe/*, delivery/*, tools/claimNextTask.ts, etc.); none are this task's three files, and none touched.

implementationPlan.description:
Phase 3 — the test first, in packages/moe-daemon/src/state/sweeps.test.ts, beside the existing 'arms one interval and genuinely clears it on stop' case. It must fail on HEAD.

Fake ONLY the interval clock: `vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ['setInterval', 'clearInterval'] })`. load() runs real fs work behind `withTimeout`, which is a setTimeout — faking every timer risks hanging the load instead of testing the sweeps.

Case 1, the defect (the card's DoD 1):
- `await h.state.load()` arms the four sweeps.
- Capture the four interval handles.
- Spy on `checkBlockedTimeouts`, `checkReconcileWindow` and `checkStaleWorkers` so a tick is observable without doing sweep work.
- Advance 4 minutes, then `await h.state.load()` again — the FileWatcher-driven reload, which the governor measured following every claim_next_task.
- Advance 1 more minute plus a second.
- Assert: each 5-minute sweep ran exactly ONCE, the 60-second watcher ran at least five times, and — the assertion that does not depend on timing at all — all four handles are the SAME objects (`toBe`) after the reload as before it.
- On HEAD both halves fail: the handles are new and the 5-minute sweeps have run zero times. Record both failure messages as the red proof.

Case 2, the guard for what must not change:
- The first load() arms all four handles (none undefined).
- `state.stop()` clears all four, and a load() after it arms four NEW handles — so the once-per-process rule does not turn a stopped daemon into a permanently unswept one.
- An explicit `startReconcileWindowCheck(h.state, 60_000)` after a load() still restarts that interval with the new cadence: the helpers keep their restart semantics for callers that mean it.

Keep the existing case untouched; it already pins arm-then-clear.

implementationPlan.description:
Phase 4 — the fix, in state/sweeps.ts and state/StateManager.ts.

(a) sweeps.ts: add `armPeriodicSweeps(state)`, which calls each `start*` ONLY when its handle is currently undefined. Document, on the function, why: a FileWatcher reload must not restart a sweep's phase, because a fleet whose reloads arrive faster than the cadence starves every self-heal behind it — the blocked-timeout alerts and parking, the resource lease reaper, the stale-worker prune, the REVIEW self-heal and the reconcile-window pass. Cite the 2026-09-17 measurement: two claims 3m59s apart reset the 5-minute timers twice without either firing, with only two active seats.

(b) StateManager.ts: replace the four calls at the end of load() with one `armPeriodicSweeps(this)`. Keep the existing comment about arming outside the locked section and about `mutex.exit`, and extend it with the once-per-process rule and why a reload needs no re-arm: the cadences are module constants and the thresholds each tick reads come from `state` at tick time, so a re-armed interval would restore nothing and only move the next tick further away.

What deliberately does NOT change:
- `start*` keeps restarting, for callers that pass a cadence on purpose.
- `stop*` and `state.stop()` are untouched, so shutdown still clears every interval and a later load() arms fresh ones.
- No sweep body, threshold or cadence changes, and nothing here touches task release (task rail 2).

Error handling: arming stays exception-free by construction and this card adds no try/catch. If `setInterval` or `mutex.exit` ever threw, the error propagates out of load() exactly as it does today — loudly. Swallowing it would be a new silent path in which the fleet runs with no self-heal at all, which is the failure this card exists to remove.

Both cases from step 2 turn green. DoD 3 is satisfied by these two comments; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md is deliberately left alone, because task-808869c5's documentation sweep owns that file right now and two cards editing it would collide.

Phase 5 — regression and mutation proof, from packages/moe-daemon.

(a) `npm test` and `npx tsc --noEmit`. The only count that may move is sweeps.test.ts. Pay attention to the suites most likely to notice a scheduling change: state/sweeps.test.ts, state/StateManager.test.ts (including 'timers armed inside runExclusive do not inherit the lock'), state/FileWatcher*.test.ts and server/*.test.ts. A moved count anywhere else means the change reached further than load()'s tail.

(b) Mutation replay in a scratch tree (mem:pattern-red-proof-by-scratch-tree-mutation-vitest), one site at a time, restoring from pristine before each, unmutated first and last:
- Restore the four `start*` calls in load(): case 1 goes red on both halves (new handles, zero ticks).
- Make `armPeriodicSweeps` arm unconditionally: same red, which proves the guard itself is what the case pins and not the refactor.
- Guard only the blocked-timeout sweep and leave the other three unconditional: case 1 goes red on the reconcile and stale assertions only — proof that each sweep is pinned separately rather than by one lucky assertion.
- Skip arming when a handle exists but never arm on the first load: case 2's 'all four armed' assertion goes red.
- Drop the `stop()` clearing: case 2's re-arm-after-stop assertion goes red.
Every failure must be behavioural, not a missing symbol.

(c) Say plainly in the step note what this fix does NOT address, so nobody reads it as more than it is: the reload rate itself is unchanged (self-write suppression is still a 500 ms per-path Set, and a claim's burst can still produce a second chokidar event), and each reload still broadcasts an unfiltered STATE_SNAPSHOT. The card scoped both out; if either still looks harmful after this lands, file it rather than widening this card. The same goes for the governor's request for a log line naming the reload's trigger path: it lives in src/index.ts, outside this card's files, and is a diagnostic rather than part of the DoD.

4. No behaviour of any sweep changed: same cadences, same thresholds, same bodies, and no idle-based release anywhere (task rail 2).
5. What is still true after this fix: reloads happen just as often, and each still broadcasts an unfiltered snapshot. Say whether you filed anything for those.
6. Would I be embarrassed if this broke in production? The worst case is a sweep that silently never arms — name the case that would catch it.

implementationPlan.note:
Self-review posted as ONE task comment (comment-6169cbaa), answering items 1-6. It covers: the mechanism now; arm-time vs tick-time values; shutdown via clearEmitter (StateManager has no stop()); the lock rules with the ALS regression test re-run; sweep behaviour unchanged, with no idle release; what remains out of scope (reload rate, unfiltered snapshot, trigger log; nothing filed); and the never-arms guard cases.
Adversarial checklist:
- Concurrent loads: armPeriodicSweeps is synchronous, so check-then-arm cannot interleave, and a second load skips armed handles (no double arming).
- clearEmitter racing an in-flight load: that load can re-arm after shutdown, exactly as before; the intervals are unref'd.
- A failed or timed-out load skips arming, as before: old handles stay armed on a reload.
- Only stop* ever set the handles to undefined, and they clear the interval first.
All theoretical and all pre-existing; none needed a change.

comments.author: worker-d0c3b06e
comments.content:
Self-review (worker-d0c3b06e), step 5

1. Mechanism, from the code as it now stands
- Before: load() ended with the four `this.start*()` calls. Each start* begins with its stop* and a fresh setInterval, and the FileWatcher callback (src/index.ts) calls `state.load()` on every unsuppressed .moe write. So every reload restarted every sweep's phase.
- Now: load() ends with `armPeriodicSweeps(this)` (state/sweeps.ts). It calls a start* only when that handle `=== undefined`, so a reload leaves an armed interval alone.
- Why nothing needs re-reading, from the step-1 walk:
  - checkBlockedTimeouts reads state.blockedTimeoutMs, reviewStaleTimeoutMs and staleWorkerTimeoutMs at TICK time.
  - checkReconcileWindow reads state.reconcileWindowMs at TICK time.
  - purgeResolvedProposals reads the module constant PROPOSAL_PURGE_AGE_MS; load() also purges inline on every load.
  - The only ARM-time capture is the stale watcher's livenessTimeoutMs. load() always armed it with the 120_000 default, so it is a constant.
  - The cadences (300000, PROPOSAL_PURGE_INTERVAL_MS, 60_000, RECONCILE_WINDOW_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS) are constants.

2. Shutdown and restart
- The plan's `state.stop()` is `clearEmitter()`: StateManager has no stop(), and index.ts shutdown calls clearEmitter. It is untouched and still clears all four handles.
- Case 'clearEmitter() stops every sweep, and the next load() arms all four again' proves the clear and the fresh re-arm. Mutants no-stop-clearing, stop-keeps-handles and module-flag all turn it red.
- Case 'an explicit start* still restarts its sweep on the cadence the caller passes' proves explicit restart semantics. Mutant idempotent-start turns it red (same handle); start-no-stop turns it red ("called 5 times, but got 6").

3. Lock rules
- armPeriodicSweeps(this) still runs after `await withTimeout(loadOperation, ...)`, where loadOperation = this.mutex.runExclusive(...), so it is outside the locked section.
- The start* bodies are unchanged and still arm via `state.mutex.exit(() => setInterval(...))`.
- Re-ran green: StateManager.test.ts 'timers armed inside runExclusive do not inherit the lock (ALS leak regression)' (StateManager.test 115/115).

4. No sweep behaviour changed. Cadences, thresholds, sweep bodies, start*/stop* bodies and clearEmitter are all byte-identical to HEAD. No idle-based release was added anywhere (rail 2). The diff is load()'s tail, one new function and tests.

5. Still true after this fix
- Reloads happen just as often: self-write suppression is still a 500 ms per-path Set, so a claim's burst can still yield a second chokidar event.
- Each reload still broadcasts an unfiltered STATE_SNAPSHOT.
- The governor's per-reload trigger log (src/index.ts) was not added.
- I filed nothing. The card scoped all three out, and after this fix they cost reload work and bandwidth, not starved self-heals.
- Note for the governor: the sweeps that a busy fleet starved (blocked-timeout parking, lease reaper, stale prune, REVIEW self-heal, reconcile pass) WILL start acting again once the daemon restarts on a rebuilt dist. Until then this is inert.

6. Embarrassment test. The worst case is a sweep that silently never arms. Four things catch it:
- case 1's `unarmed(armed)` === [];
- case 2a's all-four-armed check before and after clearEmitter (never-arm-first turns both red);
- the existing StateManager.test 'purges stale resolved proposals on load and starts purge interval';

One incident during the run: the first full `npm test` was red on stateModules.test.ts 'keeps StateManager.ts under the size budget' (1500 against a budget of <1500). My load() comment was 9 lines; I cut it to 3, and the full why lives on armPeriodicSweeps. StateManager.ts is now net +1 line (1493).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
The guard belongs at the load() call site, not inside each start*.
- `armPeriodicSweeps(state)` arms only what is unarmed; `start*` keeps restarting for callers that pass a cadence on purpose (sweeps.test.ts does exactly that, after an explicit stop).
- Rejected: making each `start*` idempotent. It would silently ignore a caller's new cadence — a trap for the next test or feature that means to re-arm — and the DoD's wording is about load(), not about the helpers.
- Rejected: arming from src/index.ts after the first load. It moves the arming away from the thing that owns the handles and leaves every other load() caller (tests, the plugin path) unswept.
- Rejected: adding try/catch around the arming. Today a failure propagates out of load() loudly; swallowing it would create a new silent path where the fleet runs with no self-heal, which is precisely this card's defect.
- Rejected here, scoped out by the card itself: tightening self-write suppression, filtering the reload snapshot, and the governor's per-reload log line (it lives in src/index.ts, outside these files).
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- load()'s tail arms four sweeps; each start* begins with its stop* and a fresh setInterval, so the phase restarts from zero on every reload. The only non-test callers of start* are those four lines.
- The existing sweeps.test.ts case 'arms one interval and genuinely clears it on stop' calls stopReconcileWindowCheck FIRST, so keeping restart semantics leaves it green.
- Cadences are module constants (RECONCILE_WINDOW_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS, 300000, 60_000, PROPOSAL_PURGE_INTERVAL_MS) and the sweep bodies read their thresholds from `state` at tick time, so a re-arm restores nothing. The one value captured at arm time is startStaleWorkerWatcher's livenessTimeoutMs — and load() always passes the default, so arming once freezes exactly what a re-arm would have restored.
- Test timing trap: load() runs real fs work behind `withTimeout`, which is a setTimeout. Fake only setInterval/clearInterval, or the load can hang instead of the sweeps being tested.
- The strongest assertion is handle identity across the reload (`toBe`), because it does not depend on the fake clock at all; the tick counts are the second, behavioural half.
planningNotes.risks:
1. A once-per-process rule must not outlive a stop(): if stop() ever stopped clearing the handles, the daemon would run unswept forever. Case 2 pins that explicitly.
2. Fake timers plus a real load() are the likely source of a flaky or hanging test; fake only the interval clock.
3. This fix does not reduce the reload rate or the unfiltered STATE_SNAPSHOT broadcast per reload. Both were scoped out by the card; say so rather than letting a reader assume the reload storm is solved.
4. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md is currently owned by task-808869c5's docs sweep, so DoD 3 is satisfied through the load() and armPeriodicSweeps comments instead.
5. The change is inert on the live fleet until the daemon is rebuilt and restarted — which is also the moment the other Wave 1 fixes activate.
